canonical_question: Why are the error bars for the neutron diffraction lattice strain measurement attributed solely to 'single-peak fitting' uncertainties?

question_variants.question: Why are the error bars for the neutron diffraction lattice strain measurement attributed solely to 'single-peak fitting' uncertainties?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper explicitly attributes the error bars for neutron diffraction lattice strain measurements to the uncertainties of the single-peak fitting on hkl diffraction peaks.

answers.answer: The text states that the error bars are obtained from the uncertainties of the single-peak fitting on hkl diffraction peaks, explaining the sole attribution of the uncertainty to this method.
answers.measurement_outcome: Error bars from single-peak fitting uncertainties
evidence_spans: The CALPHAD approach [38] – [40] is currently the only method that can be used to obtain multicomponent phase diagrams with enough accuracy for practical applications without the need of the heavy experimental work [41] .
